description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and three accuracy metrics: Initial Accuracy, Final Accuracy, and Δ Accuracy. The x-axis, labeled Initial Confidence, has a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 0.99 with a tick label interval of approximately 0.01 to 0.03. The y-axis, labeled Accuracy, also has a linear scale, spanning from 0.2 to 1.0 with a tick label interval of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: Initial Accuracy (green, dash-dot line with square markers), Final Accuracy (blue, solid line with cross markers), and Δ Accuracy (orange, dashed line with diamond markers). The Initial Accuracy line starts at around 0.5 at an Initial Confidence of 0.0 and increases to approximately 1.15 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with some fluctuations, including a notable increase between 0.84 and 0.90. The Final Accuracy line begins at around 1.05 at an Initial Confidence of 0.0 and rises to about 1.2 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with a relatively steady trend and minor fluctuations. The Δ Accuracy line starts at around 0.45 at an Initial Confidence of 0.0, decreases to approximately 0.35 at an Initial Confidence of 0.89, and then increases to around 0.65 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with some variations throughout. All three lines have error bars indicating the range of values.
